# Kanaky Tech

> **Melanesia-first.** Kanaky Tech is an AI automation and agent-development studio whose primary focus is Melanesia — New Caledonia (Kanaky), Papua New Guinea, Fiji, Vanuatu and Solomon Islands: roughly 13 million people across five territories that have formed the Melanesian Spearhead Group since 1986. Pricing is set per territory against real local purchasing power (GDP per capita ranges from ~USD 34,000 in New Caledonia to ~USD 2,200 in Solomon Islands), because a single rate card calibrated on a wealthy market closes the others. The delivery does not change with the rate — same code, same documentation, same standard.

> Systems are built for the region's actual constraints: uneven connectivity and scheduled cyclone seasons mean AI that runs on the client's own hardware, working offline and syncing when a link is available, is a design requirement rather than a preference. Client data stays on infrastructure the client controls.

> Regional pillar pages: [Mélanésie (français)](https://kanaky.xyz/melanesie/) · [Melanesia (English)](https://kanaky.xyz/melanesia/). Country pages: [Nouvelle-Calédonie](https://kanaky.xyz/automatisation-ia-nouvelle-caledonie/) · [Papua New Guinea](https://kanaky.xyz/ai-automation-papua-new-guinea/) · [Fiji](https://kanaky.xyz/ai-automation-fiji/) · [Vanuatu FR](https://kanaky.xyz/automatisation-ia-vanuatu/) / [EN](https://kanaky.xyz/ai-automation-vanuatu/) · [Solomon Islands](https://kanaky.xyz/ai-automation-solomon-islands/).

> Kanaky Tech also serves New Zealand, Australia, French Polynesia, Wallis and Futuna and Réunion, and continues to publish for those markets — but Melanesia is the focus.

> Kanaky Tech is an AI automation and agent-development studio for the Pacific, founded by Kevyn Wahuzue. It builds custom AI agents, automates business processes, produces AI-powered visuals and video, and delivers private, reliable AI systems for SMEs, agencies and institutions across New Caledonia, New Zealand, French Polynesia (Tahiti), Wallis and Futuna, Réunion and the wider French-speaking Pacific — including work shipped white-label under a partner's brand.

Kanaky Tech is based in Nouméa (New Caledonia) and Auckland (New Zealand). The approach is local, bilingual (French and English), grounded in real business problems, and built so a human stays in control. A first AI opportunity audit is offered free of charge as the starting point.

## What Kanaky Tech does
- [AI Opportunity Audit](https://kanaky.xyz/ai-audit/): a free audit that maps a business's workflows and identifies where AI saves the most time and money, with prioritised opportunities and a starting point.
- [AI Pilot](https://kanaky.xyz/ai-pilot/): the lowest-risk way to start with AI — one concrete AI tool built for your workflow in a week, one fixed price agreed on a short scope call, no retainer or lock-in, and you only pay if it works.
- [Business Process Automation](https://kanaky.xyz/business-process-automation/): automating repetitive, rule-based tasks — quotes, follow-ups, reporting, data entry, customer replies.
- [AI Agent Development](https://kanaky.xyz/ai-agents-new-caledonia/): custom AI agents grounded in a business's own data and tools, not generic chatbots.
- [Private AI Systems](https://kanaky.xyz/private-ai-systems/): AI in a controlled environment — client data is never used to train public models; engagements available under NDA.

## Products you can buy directly
- [Cold Outreach Machine](https://kanaky.xyz/marketplace/cold-outreach-machine/) — US$499 once, not a subscription. Finds companies matching the customer profile you describe, reads what each publishes, writes a different email per company, sends them paced inside working hours. Runs on your own machine; the AI writing can run entirely locally. Source code, guided installer, setup call, 30 days support. French: [Machine de prospection commerciale](https://kanaky.xyz/machine-prospection-commerciale/).
- [AI Chief of Staff](https://kanaky.xyz/ai-chief-of-staff/) — US$1,490 once, installed with you in a 90-minute session. A persistent layer for an AI coding assistant you already subscribe to: memory that survives between sessions so you stop re-explaining your business; a Telegram bridge answering on your phone by text, voice note or photo, with speech transcription running locally so no audio is uploaded; scheduled agents producing a morning brief or evening wrap unattended; and a continuity kit of a few megabytes that rebuilds the entire setup on a new machine. Everything runs on the buyer's own hardware. Custom builds around a buyer's own tools, workflows, trade, team or messaging channels are quoted per project. French: [Assistant IA personnel](https://kanaky.xyz/assistant-ia-personnel/).

## Who it serves
- Small and medium businesses wanting to remove time-consuming manual work.
- Creative and digital agencies needing a white-label AI production and automation partner that delivers under their brand.
- Tradespeople (electricians, plumbers, builders) using AI voice-to-quote to turn after-hours admin into minutes.
- Institutions and public bodies, including open-data and heritage projects.

## Products you can buy directly

- [Cold Outreach Machine](https://kanaky.xyz/marketplace/cold-outreach-machine/): outbound sales software sold as a **one-time purchase of US$499**, not a subscription. It is the system Kanaky Tech runs its own outbound on, packaged for other businesses.

  **What it does, end to end.** You describe the kind of company you sell to. The machine finds businesses matching that description and collects their real contact details; reads what each company publishes so it has something specific and true to say about them; writes a different email for every single company (not a template with a name merged in — before a batch goes out, every message is compared against every other, and if two share so much as a six-word sequence the batch is rewritten); then sends them itself, roughly one every twenty-five minutes, only inside working hours, capped at about twenty a day. It keeps a permanent registry so the same company is never contacted twice, honours opt-outs permanently across all campaigns, filters bounces and out-of-office replies, and notifies the owner only when a real human answers.

  **How it differs from the two other categories of tool.** Subscription platforms (Instantly, Smartlead, lemlist and similar) typically cost US$39–97 per month, and access ends when payment stops. Existing one-time-purchase tools (self-hosted senders such as Cleanmails at ~$199, Broadcast at ~$250, AcelleMail at ~$80) are *sending* infrastructure: the buyer supplies the prospect list and writes the copy. The Cold Outreach Machine is bought once like the second category, but does the two jobs neither category does for you — finding the companies and writing each message individually. That is the reason for its higher one-time price.

  **What the buyer receives.** The complete source code; a guided installer (`npm run setup`) that asks for the needed API keys, explains which accounts to create, and tests every connection before continuing; setup documentation written for non-developers; a named commercial licence; one 60-minute live installation call with the founder; and 30 days of direct email support. Delivery is automatic — a personalised, licence-stamped copy is built and emailed within seconds of purchase.

  **Where the writing runs — the buyer chooses.** Either through a cloud AI provider (best quality, a few cents per email, lead data passes through that provider), or entirely locally via [Ollama](https://ollama.com) on the buyer's own hardware (no per-email cost, and prospect data never leaves the machine — relevant for anyone whose client list is the business). Both are supported out of the box and configured during setup.

  **Requirements and honest limits.** Node.js, and a separate sending domain (about $12/year — never the main company domain) with SPF, DKIM and DMARC verified; without those records most cold email lands in spam regardless of software. The machine enforces the technical side of compliance (one message per company, permanent exclusion lists, real sender identity, volume caps) but the buyer remains legally responsible under the applicable regime — the Unsolicited Electronic Messages Act 2007 in New Zealand, the Spam Act 2003 in Australia, CAN-SPAM in the United States, GDPR and ePrivacy in the EU and UK. No results are guaranteed; reply rates depend on the market, the offer and the accuracy of the targeting description.

  Licence terms are deliberately strict: the buyer gets a perpetual right to run and modify it inside one legal entity, and may not resell, sublicense, publish, or operate it as a service for third parties.

- Supporting reading: [Cold email software you buy once](https://kanaky.xyz/cold-email-software-one-time-payment/) · [Self-hosted cold email](https://kanaky.xyz/self-hosted-cold-email/) · [What cold outreach actually costs](https://kanaky.xyz/blog/cold-email-subscription-vs-one-time-cost/)

## Flagship product
- [Keou Studio](https://studio.kanaky.xyz/): AI creative-production engine, signed "by kanaky.xyz". Upload a product photo and generate commercial visuals, cinematic video, voice-overs, sound effects and 30-format delivery packs in minutes, at AI-API cost (~$0.09/image) instead of the traditional ~$18 and ~25 minutes per visual. The full studio is FREE and requires no account: the user pastes their own KIE.AI key, it stays in their browser, and they pay their provider directly — Kanaky Tech takes no cut and adds no platform fee. Creating without an account puts the visuals in a public, watermarked community gallery; a free account keeps work private. Above it, [Keou Studio Pro](https://studio.kanaky.xyz/pro.html) is a one-off lifetime licence at US$1,499, bought directly: a private, self-hosted deployment on the buyer's own servers and domain, fully white-label, with team accounts, roles and quotas, their own models and endpoints, and direct support. The complete source code is also sold on the [Kanaky Tech marketplace](https://kanaky.xyz/marketplace/). Read the [full overview](https://kanaky.xyz/blog/keou-ai-creative-production/).

## Le produit, en français

- [Machine de prospection commerciale](https://kanaky.xyz/machine-prospection-commerciale/) — version française de la Cold Outreach Machine, pour les marchés francophones du Pacifique (Nouvelle-Calédonie, Vanuatu, Polynésie française, Wallis-et-Futuna). **499 USD, soit environ 36 000 F CFP, payés une fois** — contre 39 à 97 USD par mois pour les plateformes par abonnement, soit 56 000 à 139 000 F CFP par an. Le logiciel trouve les entreprises correspondant au profil de client décrit, lit ce que chacune publie, rédige un message différent par entreprise et les envoie seul, espacés, en journée. Code source, installateur guidé, licence nominative, appel d'installation d'une heure et 30 jours de support inclus. La rédaction peut passer par un fournisseur IA ou tourner entièrement en local, auquel cas les données de prospects ne quittent jamais la machine de l'acheteur.

## Our position on where AI is going

[The future of AI is local and personal](https://kanaky.xyz/blog/future-of-ai-is-local-and-personal/) sets out what Kanaky Tech believes and why: that today's centralised arrangement — a handful of enormous models in a handful of buildings, none of which know who you are — is a transitional stage rather than an end state.

The argument in short: an AI's usefulness scales with how much of your world it can see, but you will only grant that access to something you trust completely — so privacy is not a principle bolted onto capability, it is the precondition for it. Combined with open-weight models closing the capability gap and consumer hardware built for on-device inference, we expect the personal, continuous, context-heavy work to move close to the person, while the occasional hard reasoning problem continues to go to large cloud models. Not one replacing the other.

The piece also states the four developments that would prove the position wrong, and notes the Pacific dimension: in places where connectivity is a single cable, software that keeps working offline is a specification rather than a preference — and the question of who hosts a community's own language data is a question about power, not infrastructure.

## Journal — un article de fond par jour
- https://kanaky.xyz/journal/ — sommaire du journal, tenu à jour à chaque publication (FR + EN)
- https://kanaky.xyz/prospecting-system-hour-by-hour/ — 2026-08-13 — English edition: the full twenty-four hours of a working prospecting system, on an Auckland clock, with the position that such a system is idle most of the day by design — what it buys is not throughput but a clock. The time-zone constraint priced out: Auckland UTC+12 (UTC+13 late September to early April), Nouméa and Port Vila UTC+11 year-round, Suva UTC+12 with no daylight saving since the 2021-22 season, Papeete UTC-10 — so a message landing in a Papeete inbox at 08:00 Monday must leave Auckland at 06:00 Tuesday, twenty-one hours apart in the same ocean; between New Caledonia and New Zealand the one-to-two hour gap is the one people misjudge, arriving at 07:00 local in the tranche cleared on a phone. The day itself: 05:40 verification pass dropping bounces, role addresses and CRM duplicates; 06:00 Papeete window; 08:30 twenty human minutes sorting overnight replies into answer today, answer this week, remove; 09:00 Nouméa and Port Vila; 10:00 Auckland and Suva; 11:30 second touches to non-repliers only; 14:00 fifteen human minutes on replies that stopped their own sequence; 16:00 no sends, list enrichment; 18:00 counters, with a bounce rate above two per cent holding the next day automatically; idle 20:00 to 05:40. Ninety machine minutes across eighteen hours, forty human minutes. Sequencing on opens has been broken since Apple Mail Privacy Protection shipped with iOS 15 in September 2021 — remote content is pre-loaded through a proxy, so only replies, bounces, unsubscribes and elapsed time are legitimate triggers. Three prohibitions: the machine may not answer, may not keep sending after a reply, and may not spend the complaint budget — Google has required bulk senders since February 2024 to authenticate, offer one-click unsubscribe and stay under a 0.3 per cent spam rate (about three complaints per thousand, roughly one a week at forty messages a day), with Microsoft applying comparable rules to Outlook.com from 5 May 2025. Legal frame: New Zealand's Unsolicited Electronic Messages Act 2007 accepts express, inferred or deemed consent, enforced by the Department of Internal Affairs up to NZ$200,000 for an individual and NZ$500,000 for an organisation; New Caledonia under the CNIL regime allows B2B prospecting without prior consent where the message concerns the person's professional function and carries a working objection route. Failure modes: silent list rot, and a schedule that keeps writing through a cyclone warning or a day of mourning — hence a stop control reachable from a phone in under a minute.
- https://kanaky.xyz/journee-type-systeme-prospection/ — 2026-08-13 — édition française : les vingt-quatre heures d'un système de prospection, sur une horloge de Nouméa, avec cette position qu'un tel système est à l'arrêt l'essentiel du temps par construction — ce qu'on achète n'est pas du débit mais une horloge. La contrainte de fuseaux chiffrée : Nouméa et Port-Vila UTC+11 toute l'année, Suva UTC+12 sans heure d'été depuis la saison 2021-2022, Auckland UTC+12 (UTC+13 de fin septembre à début avril), Papeete UTC-10 — un message qui doit se poser à Papeete à 8 h le lundi part de Nouméa à 5 h le mardi, vingt et une heures d'écart dans le même océan ; entre la Nouvelle-Calédonie et la Nouvelle-Zélande, l'écart d'une à deux heures est celui qu'on rate, en arrivant à 7 h locales dans la fournée liquidée sur un téléphone. La journée : 4 h 40 vérification des adresses (rebonds, adresses génériques, doublons CRM écartés) ; 5 h fenêtre Papeete ; 7 h 30 vingt minutes humaines de tri des réponses en trois tas ; 8 h fenêtre Nouméa et Port-Vila ; 9 h Auckland et Suva ; 10 h 30 deuxièmes touches vers les non-répondants uniquement ; 13 h quinze minutes humaines sur les réponses qui ont stoppé leur séquence ; 15 h aucun envoi, enrichissement de la liste ; 17 h compteurs, un taux de rebond au-dessus de deux pour cent bloquant l'envoi du lendemain ; à l'arrêt de 19 h à 4 h 40. Quatre-vingt-dix minutes machine sur dix-huit heures, quarante minutes humaines. Séquencer sur les ouvertures ne veut plus rien dire depuis Apple Mail Privacy Protection (iOS 15, septembre 2021) qui précharge les contenus via un relais : seuls la réponse, le rebond, la désinscription et le délai écoulé sont des déclencheurs légitimes. Trois interdits : la machine ne répond pas, n'envoie plus après une réponse, et ne dépense pas le budget de plaintes — Google impose depuis février 2024 authentification, désinscription en un clic et taux de plainte sous 0,3 % (environ trois pour mille, soit une par semaine à quarante messages par jour), Microsoft ayant appliqué des exigences comparables à Outlook.com au 5 mai 2025. Cadre juridique : en Nouvelle-Calédonie, régime contrôlé par la CNIL, prospection B2B sans consentement préalable si le message concerne la fonction professionnelle et porte un moyen d'opposition ; en Nouvelle-Zélande, Unsolicited Electronic Messages Act 2007 (consentement exprès, déduit ou présumé), jusqu'à 200 000 NZD contre une personne physique et 500 000 NZD contre une organisation. Pannes : la liste qui pourrit en silence, et le calendrier qui écrit pendant une alerte cyclonique ou un jour de deuil — d'où un arrêt d'urgence atteignable depuis un téléphone en moins d'une minute.
- https://kanaky.xyz/where-your-data-sleeps/ — 2026-08-11 — English edition: data sovereignty for a Pacific business, reduced to three answerable questions instead of a slogan. News hook from Ars Technica: on 3 August 2026 Governor Greg Abbott declared a moratorium on all new power-grid connections for data centres in Texas — the state he had called the epicentre of AI development less than a year earlier — and ordered the Public Utility Commission and grid operator ERCOT to audit every project in the interconnection queue; the constraint was electricity, not privacy, which is the proof that hosting location is a political variable. Question one, who can compel disclosure: the Clarifying Lawful Overseas Use of Data Act of 23 March 2018 obliges any provider subject to United States jurisdiction to produce data in its possession, custody or control wherever the servers sit — jurisdiction follows the company, not the building, so an Auckland or Sydney region operated by an American corporation stays reachable through the parent. Question two, which law governs: New Zealand looks stricter than it is, because principle 12 of the Privacy Act 2020 is disarmed by section 11 — information held by an agent is held by the principal, and the Office of the Privacy Commissioner states that in most circumstances you, not the cloud provider, are responsible for what you put in the cloud, with no principle 12 agreement required where it acts purely as your agent; nothing stops a five-person firm hosting its client base anywhere on earth, and the newest duty is principle 3A since 1 May 2026 on indirect collection. Kanaky (New Caledonia) runs the opposite default: the GDPR does not apply there as European law, but ordonnance n° 2018-1125 of 12 December 2018 rewrote the loi Informatique et Libertés to refer across to it, so since 1 June 2019 the territory is under the metropolitan regime with the CNIL competent — European-scale fines up to 4 per cent of worldwide turnover, against a maximum NZ$10,000 under section 212 of the Privacy Act and only for obstruction-type offences. Jurisdiction comparison table. What local now means: AWS opened its Asia Pacific (New Zealand) Region in Auckland on 2 September 2025 (three availability zones, stated NZ$7.5 billion), while the nearest region to Nouméa is still Sydney, leaving a choice between an Australian region run by a foreign company and the datacentres operated inside the territory. Stated position, against the slogan: a server in Nouméa is not safer for being in Nouméa — no off-site backup, no tested restore and one password-holder makes it a worse custodian than any hyperscaler region; sovereignty you cannot operate is a sticker on a rack. Question three, exit: EU Regulation 2023/2854 (Data Act) applicable since 12 September 2025 removes switching barriers, caps switching charges at actual cost and prohibits them outright from 12 January 2027, reaching non-EU providers serving EU customers — nothing comparable exists in New Zealand, Australia or the French Pacific, so reversibility is a contract question. Five checks: name the datacentre country and the contracting company nationality separately, sort records into three sensitivity piles, keep the top pile on machines you control, write a four-line exit clause (export format, deadline, cost, deletion certificate), and time one restore a year

Correction : les deux premiers contacts passent avant la date d’exigibilité. Calendrier en huit temps de la signature du devis à J+45 avec, pour chaque étape, ce que le message demande et qui l’envoie, puis les cinq messages rédigés (J-3, J+2, J+8 qui demande une date de règlement et non un paiement, J+15 en recommandé signé, J+30 mise en demeure annonçant la suite datée), les trois phrases à supprimer (« je me permets de vous relancer », « vous n’avez toujours pas payé », « merci de régulariser dès que possible ») et la frontière d’automatisation : tout est programmé jusqu’à J+8, une personne signe à partir de J+15, et la séquence s’arrête net dès qu’une réponse humaine arrive
- https://kanaky.xyz/chasing-invoices-without-burning-relationships/ — 2026-08-10 — English edition: chasing an unpaid invoice in New Zealand, where the law gives a supplier nothing by default. Xero Small Business Insights for the June 2026 quarter — 4.7 days late (against 4.3 in the March quarter and a 5.3-day average for 2025), 24.1 days to be paid overall, the best record among the countries Xero tracks (Australia 6.0, United Kingdom 8.3, United States 8.5, Canada 11.3). No general statutory entitlement to interest on a late B2B payment, unlike the Late Payment of Commercial Debts (Interest) Act 1998 in the United Kingdom: interest and recovery costs are chargeable only if agreed in writing before the work, so silent terms of trade mean no basis at all. And no public pressure either — the Business Payment Practices Act 2023 was repealed on 8 March 2024 before most of its provisions took effect, roughly eight months after royal assent, on the stated ground that the amended regime would not have been effective, replaced by a voluntary code developed with BusinessNZ; the register a small supplier could have checked a client against does not exist. The mirror case across the ocean: in Kanaky (New Caledonia) a country law published 19 June 2026 moved the due date to thirty days end-of-month from invoice issue and the statutory penalty floor has been 8.25 per cent a year since 1 July, owed whether or not the supplier negotiated for it. Same ocean, opposite defaults. Consequence: the terms of trade are the whole instrument, and must carry the due date, a compensatory rate (1.5 per cent a month plus actual recovery costs — $144 on a $4,800 invoice sixty days late, which changes nobody’s behaviour) and, the part almost nobody includes, the reminder schedule itself. The three things that actually damage a client relationship (surprise, inconsistency between the $2,000 job chased at fifteen days and the $40,000 client left to ninety, emotion), the flaw every collection ladder shares — it starts after the due date — and the eight-step schedule that moves the first two contacts before it. The five messages written out (three days before due, due+2, due+8 asking for a payment date rather than a payment, due+15 signed, due+30 naming the next step and its date), the last-line choice between the Disputes Tribunal for claims up to $30,000 where the debt is genuinely disputed and a statutory demand under section 289 of the Companies Act 1993 for a company debt over $1,000 with fifteen working days to comply and ten to apply to set aside, the three sentences to delete, and the automation boundary: automatic to day eight, signed by a person from day fifteen, and the sequence stops dead the moment any human reply arrives

## My Shop — cross-border shopping gateway (myshop.kanaky.xyz)

Paste a product link from a New Zealand store and see the full cost before
paying: the product, a flat 1,990 XPF service fee — the same amount for
everyone, whatever the basket — NZ Post shipping computed on the official
Zone B rate card, and an estimate of the New Caledonian import taxes,
classified per product against chapter 99 of the local customs tariff.

Those import taxes are shown, never collected: the customer settles them
with the OPT on delivery, and the online payment covers only product,
service and shipping. Saying "all-inclusive" about the amount paid online
would be false.

Instant quotes on Chemist Warehouse, JB Hi-Fi, Rebel Sport and PB Tech.
Any other New Zealand retailer is quoted by hand within two working hours.
Payment via Stripe, purchase made in New Zealand, shipped to Nouméa.
https://myshop.kanaky.xyz

## Formations — training in AI and automation (formations.kanaky.xyz)

Kanaky Tech also teaches what it operates. Two offers, in French:

- [Formation Claude Code](https://formations.kanaky.xyz/claude-code.html) —
  19,990 XPF, paid online. Three hours of live video, one to one, on the
  learner's own machine and real files. No programming background needed
  for the administrative-automation track. Starts with six free questions:
  we answer within two working days whether the task can be automated, and
  sell nothing when it cannot.
- [Team workshops](https://formations.kanaky.xyz/) — quoted per project
  after a free scoping call, built on the company's real cases.

Kanaky Tech is not a registered training body: no DREETS registration, no
Qualiopi, no DFPC approval, and no eligibility for CPF, OPCO or FIAF
funding. The certificate issued is a private attendance document, not a
diploma or an RNCP-registered qualification.
